description: Master var, let, const, block scope, function scope, and Temporal Dead Zone gotchas.

questions.title: Predict Output: var scoping vs let scoping inside loops
questions.question: What will be printed when running `for(var i=0; i<3; i++) { setTimeout(()=>console.log(i), 100); }` vs using `let i`?
questions.solution: With `var`, it prints `3 3 3` because `var` is function-scoped and shares 1 binding. With `let`, it prints `0 1 2` because `let` creates a new block-scoped binding for each loop iteration.

questions.title: Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) Identification
questions.question: Why does accessing `let a` before line `let a = 10` throw ReferenceError while `var b` returns `undefined`?
questions.solution: `let` and `const` are hoisted into the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) from the start of the block until execution reaches their declaration line. Accessing them in TDZ throws ReferenceError.

questions.title: Const Mutation Trap
questions.question: Can you push elements into an array declared with `const arr = []`? Why or why not?
questions.solution: Yes! `const` prevents re-assigning the variable identifier reference (`arr = newArr`), but it does NOT freeze internal object/array mutations.

questions.title: Global Window Pollution
questions.question: Which keyword (`var`, `let`, `const`) attaches variables declared at top-level to the global `window` object in browser?
questions.solution: `var` attaches to `window` (e.g. `var x = 5` -> `window.x === 5`). `let` and `const` do NOT attach to the global object.

questions.title: Redeclaration Rules
questions.question:
Which of the following will throw a SyntaxError?
A) `var a=1; var a=2;` 
B) `let b=1; let b=2;`
questions.solution: Option B throws `SyntaxError: Identifier 'b' has already been declared`. `let` cannot be re-declared within the same scope.

questions.title: Shadowing & Block Scope
questions.question: What is variable shadowing? Can a `var` shadow a `let` variable in a nested block?
questions.solution: Shadowing occurs when an inner scope variable has the same name as outer scope. Illegal shadowing: A `var` CANNOT shadow a `let` in the same/nested scope, but `let` CAN shadow `var`.

questions.title: Freeze Object Immutability (Interview Classic)
questions.question: How do you make an object completely immutable in JavaScript so properties cannot be added, edited, or deleted?
questions.solution: Use `Object.freeze(obj)`. For deep nested objects, implement a recursive `deepFreeze(obj)` function.

questions.title: Implement a Const-like Wrapper Function
questions.question: Write a function `createImmutableProp(obj, propName, value)` using `Object.defineProperty` to make a read-only property.

description: Master primitives vs references, type coercion, IEEE 754 precision, and NaN checks.

questions.title: The `typeof null` Historical Bug
questions.question: What does `typeof null` return, and why?
questions.solution: It returns `"object"`. This is a legacy bug from JS 1.0 where type tags for objects were represented as 0, and `null` was represented as NULL pointer (0x00).

questions.title: Coercion Matrix: `"5" + 3` vs `"5" - 3`
questions.question: Evaluate: `console.log("5" + 3)` and `console.log("5" - 3)`.
questions.solution:
`"5" + 3 === "53"` (+ triggers string concatenation if either operand is String).
`"5" - 3 === 2` (- converts string to number).

questions.title: NaN Comparison Traps
questions.question: Why does `NaN === NaN` evaluate to `false`? How do you reliably check for NaN?
questions.solution: `NaN` (Not-a-Number) is the only value in JS not equal to itself. Use `Number.isNaN(val)` or `Object.is(val, NaN)`.

questions.title: Floating Point Precision Gotcha
questions.question: Why does `0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3` return `false`? How do you compare floating points safely?
questions.solution: JS uses IEEE 754 64-bit float format. `0.1 + 0.2` equals `0.30000000000000004`. Compare using epsilon: `Math.abs(a - b) < Number.EPSILON`.

questions.title: Loose vs Strict Equality Matrix
questions.question: Evaluate: A) `false == 0`  B) `"" == 0`  C) `null == undefined`  D) `null === undefined`
questions.solution: A) true  B) true  C) true  D) false (Loose equality `==` coerces types; `null` only loosely equals `undefined`).

questions.title: Explicit Type Conversions
questions.question: Write a snippet converting string `"123.45px"` into a clean number `123.45`.
questions.solution: Use `parseFloat("123.45px")` -> `123.45`. Note: `Number("123.45px")` returns `NaN`.

questions.title: BigInt & Safe Integer Bounds
questions.question: What is `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`? How do you perform operations on integers larger than 2^53 - 1?
questions.solution: `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is `9007199254740991`. For larger numbers, use BigInt literals (append `n` to integer e.g., `9007199254740993n`).

questions.title: Symbol Property Privacy & Uniqueness
questions.question: Are Symbols unique? Does `Symbol("id") === Symbol("id")` evaluate to true or false?
questions.solution: Every Symbol call returns a guaranteed unique Symbol value. `Symbol("id") === Symbol("id")` is `false`. Useful for hidden object properties.

description: Master string immutability, slice vs substring, template literals, and regex patterns.

questions.title: String Immutability Proof
questions.question: If `let str = 'hello'`, what happens when executing `str[0] = 'H'`?
questions.solution: Nothing! Strings in JS are immutable. `str` remains `'hello'`. In strict mode (`'use strict'`), it throws an error.

questions.title: Reverse a String (3 Ways)
questions.question: Write a 1-line function to reverse a string `'FocusFlow'`.

questions.title: Slice vs Substring Difference
questions.question: What does `'JavaScript'.slice(-4)` return vs `'JavaScript'.substring(-4)`?
questions.solution:
`'JavaScript'.slice(-4)` returns `'ript'` (supports negative index from end).
`'JavaScript'.substring(-4)` treats negative index as `0`, returning `'JavaScript'`.

questions.title: Palindrome Checker Function
questions.question: Write a function `isPalindrome(str)` ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters.

questions.title: Title Case Capitalization
questions.question: Write a function `toTitleCase("chai aur code")` returning `"Chai Aur Code"`.

questions.title: Count Vowels in a String
questions.question: Count vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in string `"javascript exercises"`.

questions.title: First Non-Repeating Character
questions.question: Find the first character in string `"abacddbec"` that does not repeat.

questions.title: Truncate String with Ellipsis
questions.question: Write `truncateStr(str, num)` that truncates string to length `num` and appends `...` if longer.

description: Master map, filter, reduce, splice vs slice, flat, and array deduplication.

questions.title: Deduplicate Array Items (4 Ways)
questions.question: Write the cleanest 1-liner to remove duplicates from `[1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5]`.

questions.title: Splice vs Slice Mutability Check
questions.question: Given `arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, what is the difference between `arr.slice(1, 3)` and `arr.splice(1, 3)`?
questions.solution:
`slice(1, 3)` returns `[2, 3]` without altering `arr`.
`splice(1, 3)` removes 3 elements starting at index 1 (`[2, 3, 4]`) and MUTATES `arr` to `[1, 5]`.

questions.title: Map vs Filter vs Reduce Purpose
questions.question: Which method would you use to A) Calculate total price of shopping cart, B) Get products with price > $50, C) Format all price numbers with $ sign?
questions.solution:
A) `reduce()` (Accumulate single total value)
B) `filter()` (Select subset matching criteria)
C) `map()` (Transform each element)

questions.title: Flatten Multidimensional Array
questions.question: Flatten deeply nested array `[1, [2, [3, [4]]]]` into single flat array `[1, 2, 3, 4]`.
questions.solution: Use `arr.flat(Infinity)` or recursive custom function.

questions.title: Implement Custom `myMap` Prototype
questions.question: Write a custom `Array.prototype.myMap` implementation without using built-in `.map()`.

questions.title: Find Two Sum Indices (LeetCode #1)
questions.question: Given `nums = [2, 7, 11, 15]` and `target = 9`, return indices of 2 numbers adding up to target in O(n) time.

questions.title: Group Objects by Property with Reduce
questions.question: Given `users = [{age:20, name:'A'}, {age:20, name:'B'}, {age:30, name:'C'}]`, group users by age.

questions.title: Array Sort Mutability & Comparator Gotcha
questions.question: Why does `[10, 5, 20, 2].sort()` produce `[10, 20, 2, 5]`? How do you sort numerically?
questions.solution: Default `.sort()` converts elements to strings and compares UTF-16 code units. For numbers, pass comparator: `arr.sort((a, b) => a - b)`.

description: Master object literals, keys/values/entries, shallow vs deep clone, and destructuring.

questions.title: Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy Methods
questions.question: What is the difference between `Object.assign({}, obj)` and `structuredClone(obj)`?
questions.solution:
`Object.assign` and spread `{...obj}` create a SHALLOW copy (nested objects share reference).
`structuredClone()` creates a true DEEP copy including nested objects/dates/maps.

questions.title: Object Destructuring with Default & Alias
questions.question: Destructure `name` as `userName` and `role` with default `'Student'` from `const person = { name: 'Ali' }`.

questions.title: Check if Property Exists in Object
questions.question: What is the difference between `'key' in obj` and `obj.hasOwnProperty('key')`?
questions.solution:
`'key' in obj` checks both object AND its prototype chain.
`obj.hasOwnProperty('key')` checks ONLY object's own direct properties.

questions.title: Count Frequency of Words in Object
questions.question: Write a function `countWords(['apple', 'banana', 'apple'])` returning `{apple: 2, banana: 1}`.

questions.title: Invert Object Keys and Values
questions.question: Write a function `invertObj({a: '1', b: '2'})` returning `{'1': 'a', '2': 'b'}`.

questions.title: Optional Chaining & Nullish Coalescing
questions.question: Rewrite safely without errors: `const city = user && user.address && user.address.city || 'Unknown'` using ES2020 syntax.

questions.title: Implement Custom `deepEqual(obj1, obj2)`
questions.question: Write a function to recursively compare 2 objects for deep structural equality.
questions.solution: Compare keys length, then recursively verify `typeof` and values equality for every key.

questions.title: Property Descriptor Configuration
questions.question: How do you prevent a property from showing up in `for...in` loops or `Object.keys()`?
questions.solution: Set `enumerable: false` using `Object.defineProperty(obj, prop, { enumerable: false })`.

description: Master declarations vs expressions, parameter defaults, rest parameters, and IIFEs.

questions.title: Declaration vs Expression Hoisting
questions.question: Why does calling `foo()` work before declaration, but calling `bar()` throws `TypeError: bar is not a function`?
questions.solution:
`function foo() {}` declaration hoists both name and function body.
`var bar = function() {}` hoists variable `bar` as `undefined`.

questions.title: Rest Parameters vs Arguments Object
questions.question: Why are Rest parameters (`...args`) preferred over the legacy `arguments` keyword?
questions.solution:
1. `...args` is a real Array (supports map/filter/reduce), whereas `arguments` is an Array-like object.
2. `...args` works cleanly in Arrow functions.

questions.title: Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE)
questions.question: Write an IIFE syntax and explain why IIFEs were historically used in JS modules.

questions.title: First-Class Functions & Callbacks
questions.question: What makes JavaScript functions 'First-Class Citizens'?
questions.solution: Functions can be assigned to variables, passed as arguments to other functions, and returned from functions.

questions.title: Pure Functions & Side Effects
questions.question: What is a Pure Function? Which of these is pure: A) `Math.random()` B) `(a, b) => a + b`?
questions.solution: A pure function always returns same output for same inputs and has NO side effects. Option B is pure; Option A is impure.

questions.title: Currying Function Implementation
questions.question: Write a curried function `add(2)(3)(4)` that returns `9`.

questions.title: Infinite Currying Function (Interview Favorite)
questions.question: Implement an infinite currying sum function `sum(1)(2)(3)...()` that returns total when invoked empty.

questions.title: Function Debounce Implementation
questions.question: Write a `debounce(fn, delay)` function to rate-limit search input handlers.

description: Master dynamic this binding, explicit binding (call/apply/bind), and arrow function lexicals.

questions.title: 4 Rules of `this` Binding
questions.question: List the 4 rules that determine what `this` points to in JS.
questions.solution:
1. Default binding (standalone call -> window/undefined)
2. Implicit binding (object method `obj.method()`) 
3. Explicit binding (`call`/`apply`/`bind`)
4. New binding (`new Constructor()`)

questions.title: Call vs Apply vs Bind Differences
questions.question: What is the difference between `fn.call()`, `fn.apply()`, and `fn.bind()`?
questions.solution:
`call(thisArg, arg1, arg2)`: Invokes immediately with comma args.
`apply(thisArg, [arg1, arg2])`: Invokes immediately with array args.
`bind(thisArg, arg1)`: Returns a NEW bound function without executing immediately.

questions.title: Arrow Functions Lexical `this` Trap
questions.question: Predict output of `user = { name:'A', say: () => console.log(this.name) }; user.say();`
questions.solution: Prints `undefined` (or global name). Arrow functions do NOT have `this` — they inherit `this` lexically from outer window scope.

questions.title: Method Borrowing with `call()`
questions.question: Borrow `Array.prototype.slice` to convert arguments object into real Array.

questions.title: Implement Custom `myBind()` Prototype
questions.question: Write custom `Function.prototype.myBind` without using built-in `.bind()`.

questions.title: Losing `this` in Callback Timeout
questions.question: Why does `setTimeout(user.sayHi, 1000)` lose `this` context? Fix it 2 ways.
questions.solution:
When passed as callback, method loses object context.
Fix 1: `setTimeout(() => user.sayHi(), 1000)`
Fix 2: `setTimeout(user.sayHi.bind(user), 1000)`

questions.title: `new` Keyword 4-Step Process
questions.question: What 4 steps happen when executing `new Person('Sameed')`?
questions.solution:
1. Creates empty object `{}`.
2. Links `__proto__` to `Person.prototype`.
3. Binds `this` to new object and executes constructor.
4. Returns new object (unless constructor explicitly returns another object).

questions.title: Chaining Methods with `this`
questions.question: How do you make a calculator object `calc.add(5).subtract(2).getResult()` chainable?
questions.solution: Return `this` at the end of each chainable method: `add(n) { this.val += n; return this; }`.

description: Master outer lexical environment access, private variables, and closure memory leaks.

questions.title: Closure Definition & Core Mechanism
questions.question: Define closure in 1 simple sentence.
questions.solution: A closure is a function bundled together with references to its outer lexical environment, preserving variables even after the outer function finishes execution.

questions.title: Private Counter Pattern
questions.question: Create a `createCounter()` function with private `count` variable and `increment()`, `decrement()`, `getCount()` methods.

questions.title: Closure Loop Bug Fix (Classic)
questions.question: Fix bug: `for(var i=0; i<3; i++) { setTimeout(()=>console.log(i), 100); }` using closure (WITHOUT changing `var` to `let`).

questions.title: Function Memoization using Closure
questions.question: Write a `memoize(fn)` wrapper that caches calculated results for expensive operations.

questions.title: Module Pattern with Closures
questions.question: How do closures enable Encapsulation and Data Privacy in JavaScript modules?
questions.solution: Variables declared inside outer function are inaccessible from outside scope. Only methods exposed via returned object can read/write those closed variables.

questions.title: Run Once Function (`once`)
questions.question: Write a function `once(fn)` that ensures `fn` is executed only once no matter how many times called.

questions.title: Closure Memory Leak Prevention
questions.question: How can closures cause memory leaks in single-page web applications?
questions.solution: If a closure retains references to large DOM elements or arrays, the Garbage Collector cannot free them even when no longer displayed. Nullify unused variables when done.

questions.title: Partial Application Function
questions.question: Write `partial(fn, ...presetArgs)` that pre-fills arguments using closures.

description: Master microtasks vs macrotasks, Promise states, async/await, and Promise combinators.

questions.title: Event Loop Task Queue Order (Interview Classic)
questions.question:
Predict output order: 
`console.log(1); setTimeout(()=>console.log(2),0); Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log(3)); console.log(4);`
questions.solution:
Prints: `1, 4, 3, 2`.
Synchronous code (1, 4) executes first. Microtask Promise queue (3) runs before Macrotask setTimeout queue (2).

questions.title: Promise States & Immutability
questions.question: What happens if a Promise calls `resolve('A')` followed immediately by `reject('B')`?
questions.solution: The Promise resolves to `'A'`. Once a Promise state transitions from Pending to Fulfilled or Rejected, it becomes immutable and subsequent calls are ignored.

questions.title: Promise.all vs Promise.allSettled
questions.question: If 1 of 5 promises rejects, what is the output of `Promise.all()` vs `Promise.allSettled()`?
questions.solution:
`Promise.all()` rejects immediately with the error of the first rejected promise (short-circuit).
`Promise.allSettled()` waits for all promises and returns an array of objects describing status (`fulfilled`/`rejected`) of each.

questions.title: Retry Failed API Request
questions.question: Write `fetchWithRetry(url, retries)` that retries failed fetch up to `retries` times before rejecting.

questions.title: Sleep / Delay Helper Function
questions.question: Write a `sleep(ms)` helper function using Promises so you can execute `await sleep(2000)`.

questions.title: Sequential vs Parallel Async Execution
questions.question: Given `[url1, url2, url3]`, write parallel fetch vs sequential fetch using async/await.
questions.solution:
Parallel: `await Promise.all(urls.map(url => fetch(url)))`
Sequential: Use a `for...of` loop with `await fetch(url)` inside.

questions.title: Custom Promise Implementation (Simplified)
questions.question: Write a mini `MyPromise` class supporting `.then()` and `resolve()`.
questions.solution: Implement state `PENDING/FULFILLED`, `value`, and `callbacks` array invoked when state transitions.

questions.title: Promise.race vs Promise.any
questions.question: What is the difference between `Promise.race()` and `Promise.any()`?
questions.solution:
`Promise.race()` settles (fulfills or rejects) as soon as FIRST promise settles.
`Promise.any()` fulfills as soon as FIRST promise FULFILLS (ignores rejections unless all reject).

description: Master DOM tree traversal, event bubbling, event delegation, and performance optimization.

questions.title: Event Bubbling vs Capturing
questions.question: Explain Event Bubbling vs Capturing. Which direction does Bubbling propagate?
questions.solution: Bubbling propagates UPWARDS from the target element to window. Capturing propagates DOWNWARDS from window to target element.

questions.title: Event Delegation Pattern (Interview Classic)
questions.question: Why is adding 1 event listener to `<ul>` better than adding 100 listeners to `<li>` items?
questions.solution: Event Delegation uses bubbling. 1 listener on `<ul>` handles clicks for all current AND dynamically added `<li>` elements, saving memory and DOM setup overhead.

questions.title: NodeList vs HTMLCollection
questions.question: What is the key difference between `querySelectorAll` (NodeList) and `getElementsByTagName` (HTMLCollection)?
questions.solution: `querySelectorAll` returns a static NodeList (supports `.forEach()`). `getElementsByTagName` returns a LIVE HTMLCollection that auto-updates when DOM changes.

questions.title: preventDefault vs stopPropagation
questions.question: What is the difference between `e.preventDefault()` and `e.stopPropagation()`?
questions.solution:
`e.preventDefault()` cancels browser default action (e.g. link navigation/form submit).
`e.stopPropagation()` stops event from bubbling up the DOM tree.

questions.title: Dynamic Element Creation & Insertion
questions.question: Write code to create `<button class='btn'>Click</button>` and append to `<div id='app'>`.

questions.title: Reflow & Repaint Optimization (DocumentFragment)
questions.question: How do you append 1,000 `<li>` items to a `<ul>` without causing 1,000 DOM reflows?

questions.title: Form Submit Handler without Reload
questions.question: Write event listener for `<form id='login'>` to prevent page reload and log form inputs.

questions.title: Intersection Observer API for Infinite Scroll
questions.question: How do you detect when a sentinel `<div>` at the bottom of the page becomes visible?
